description: "Balance of Power: Late Edition" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Daniel Kurtzer, Former US Ambassador to Israel during the George W. Bush Administration, discusses the uncertainty around a potential deal with Iran. Republican Senator Mike Rounds of South Dakota addresses ongoing DHS funding negotiations and President Donald Trump's push to link funding with voter ID requirements. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US, Iran at Odds Over Whether Truce Talks Are Happening | Balance of Power: Late Edition 03/23/26

author: Nick Wadhams
description: The Defense Department will no longer allow media organizations to keep offices in the Pentagon building after a federal judge ruled that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had improperly revoked credentials for dozens of them.
title: Pentagon, After Court Loss, Will Bar Media Offices From Building

author: Zoe Tillman
description: A federal judge in Washington will allow a lawsuit to go forward that accuses billionaire Elon Musk of unconstitutionally exercising executive power during his time in the Trump administration last year as a presidential adviser.
title: Musk Must Face Suit Alleging Power Overreach as Trump Adviser

author: Kate O'Keeffe, Mark Gurman
description: The Federal Communications Commission ordered a ban on the import of new models of foreign-produced consumer wireless routers after an interagency panel determined they threaten national security.
title: FCC Bans Wireless Router Imports, Citing Security Concerns

description: Republican Senator Mike Rounds of South Dakota discusses whether Congress has been briefed on US-Iran negotiations, the potential need for supplemental funding, and concerns around Iran's missile capabilities targeting the US and its allies. He also addresses ongoing DHS funding negotiations and President Donald Trump's push to link funding with voter ID requirements. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Rounds on Iran Talks, Missile Threats, DHS Funding

author: Lynn Doan
description: Dragos Inc., a cybersecurity firm that’s contracted to do business with US government agencies, won’t halt its use of Anthropic PBC’s artificial intelligence products unless formally told by the government to stop, according to the company’s chief executive officer.
title: Dragos Chief Says He Won’t Stop Using Anthropic Unless Ordered

description: Daniel Kurtzer, Former US Ambassador to Israel during the George W. Bush Administration, discusses the uncertainty around a potential deal with Iran, the challenges of securing and removing enriched uranium, and differing US-Israel perspectives on ending the conflict. He also addresses the role of intermediaries and the complexity of ongoing negotiations. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on the late edition of Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Fmr. Ambassador to Israel on Iran Deal Prospects, Israeli Objectives

author: Nancy Cook
description: The administration is soliciting ideas to bring some relief at the gas pump
title: Trump Team Hunts for Ways to Blunt Gas Price Increases

author: Erin Hudson
description: Residents of Montclair, New Jersey, voted in favor of a one-time tax increase to help their cash-strapped public school system address a nearly $18 million deficit.
title: Montclair Approves One-Time Tax Hike for Schools in Close Vote

description: On today's episode of Bloomberg Businessweek Daily, Carol Massar and Tim Stenovec speak with Bloomberg News Middle East & North Africa Managing Editor Onur Ant and Bloomberg News White House and National Security Editor Michelle Jamrisko as the US and Iran remain at odds over whether truce talks are happening. Then, Bloomberg News Managing Editor for Global Consumer Tech Mark Gurman joins to discuss his Big Take story about Apple's heir apparent John Ternus. Plus, TD Securities Head of FX Strategy Jayati Bharadwaj joins to discuss the dollar's decline amid back and forth about Iran talks and President Trump's pullback on striking Iranian energy targets. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Stocks Higher as Trump Backs Off Iran Threats | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 3/23/2026

author: Liam Knox
description: The Trump administration said Monday it has launched two new investigations into Harvard University over alleged antisemitism on campus and racially discriminatory admissions practices.
title: Harvard Faces New Civil Rights Probes From Trump Administration

author: Amara Omeokwe
description: The ongoing legal standoff between the Trump administration and Federal Reserve is increasing the likelihood that the next Fed chief won’t be confirmed by the Senate before Chair Jerome Powell’s term ends in May.
title: Trump Wants Powell Out, But What Happens If Warsh Isn't Confirmed in Time?

author: Zoltan Simon
description: Hungarian opposition leader Peter Magyar said he will oust Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s key allies — including the president and chief justices — if his party wins a supermajority in elections on April 12.
title: Magyar Vows to Oust Orban’s Allies If He Wins Hungarian Vote

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from the Middle East. On today's show, Aspen Strategy Group Executive Director Anja Manuel, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and former Congresswoman Jane Harman. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Backs Off From Iran Threat | Balance of Power: Early Edition 3/23/2026

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Giorgia Meloni and her allies were upbeat in the runup to a referendum to overhaul the justice system that they expected would reaffirm their power a year ahead of a national election.
title: Meloni Hits a Sudden Hurdle on Way to Re-Election Campaign

author: Patrick Van Oosterom
description: The Dutch Finance Ministry said it had blocked access to some of its computer systems after a hack was detected on March 19.
title: Dutch Finance Ministry Blocks Computer Systems After Hack

author: Maggie Eastland, Carmen Arroyo
description: Silicon Valley’s alliance with the Trump administration will be on display Tuesday at a summit in Washington where business leaders’ calls to keep the US lead in artificial intelligence will be tested by growing public concern over AI’s economic impact and its use in the Iran war.
title: Silicon Valley’s DC Summit Shadowed by AI Concerns, War in Iran

author: Ari Natter
description: US President Donald Trump’s energy chief downplayed the impact the US-Israeli war with Iran is having on energy markets, saying prices haven’t risen enough to trigger “meaningful demand destruction.”
title: Trump’s Energy Boss Plays Down Price Shock From Iran Conflict

description:
President Trump says talks with Iran started after the US threatened to strike energy sites. 
Trump says that talks started “last night, a little bit the night before that”   The President also spoke on voter verification stating he will be 'tying' voter is and DHS funding together. He spoke at the Memphis Safe Task Force Roundtable in Memphis Tennessee. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran Talks Started After Energy Strikes Threat Says Trump (Opening Remarks)

author: Maggie Eastland, Carmen Arroyo
description: The US plans to contribute $250 million toward an investment consortium that would help fund projects aimed at strengthening supply chains for energy and critical minerals, according to a Trump administration official.
title: US to Commit $250 Million Toward Supply Chain Investment Fund

author: Alan Crawford, Galit Altstein
description: It’s been half a century since the Vietnam War, when journalists had almost unrestricted access to the battlefield.
title: Iran Is the First War of the Social-Media Age. It’s a Black Box

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy, Skylar Woodhouse
description: President Donald Trump urged Republican lawmakers to link funds to reopen the Department of Homeland Security to voter ID legislation and remain in Washington through the Easter holiday if needed — imploring them to “make this one for Jesus.”
title: Trump Calls for Tying Voter ID to DHS Funds in Shutdown Fight

author: Galit Altstein
description: Israel lost 8.6% of annual gross domestic product, or 177 billion shekels ($57 billion), during the two years through 2025, figures that demonstrate the economic toll of the country’s state of near constant conflict.
title: Israel Says Economy Lost Over $57 Billion During Two Years of War in Gaza

author: Greg Stohr
description: The US Supreme Court signaled a divide over Republican calls to require mail-in ballots to arrive by Election Day, with key justices voicing concern about the impact the case might have on the practice of early voting.
title: Supreme Court Signals Divide on Election-Day Ballot Deadline

author: Liam Knox
description: Colleges are racing to comply with President Donald Trump’s demand for sweeping admissions data and bracing for those records to fuel a new crackdown on campus diversity efforts. They face a Wednesday deadline to submit these documents, even as a federal judge considers whether that mandate is enforceable.
title: Trump’s Demand for Admissions Data Sends Wary Colleges Scrambling

author: Samy Adghirni
description: The leaders of the far-right National Rally have said 2027 will be the year they finally win France’s presidential election. But in Sunday’s municipal runoffs, the party struggled in several cities to turn strong initial results into victories.
title: French Election Runoffs Show Far Right Still Has Work to Do

author: Jorge Valero, Oliver Crook
description: US Ambassador to the European Union Andrew Puzder warned the bloc should expect more tariffs if it doesn’t approve a stalled trade deal with Washington.
title: US Envoy Says EU Faces Higher Tariffs if Trade Deal Fails

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump said the US would postpone strikes against Iran’s energy infrastructure after what he called “productive conversations” with the country, in comments that spurred confusion over the participants in the talks and parameters of a deal.
title: Trump Touts Fresh Iran Talks, Delays Attacks on Energy Sites

author: Maeve Sheehey
description: A once-bipartisan effort to create a Smithsonian women’s history museum has fallen victim to familiar partisan fights over transgender inclusion and President Donald Trump’s power.
title: Women’s History Museum Bill Stalls on Trump, Transgender Fights

author: Joe Mayes
description: Keir Starmer said he is looking at wider measures to support Britain’s economy through the Iran crisis as he prepares to chair an emergency meeting on the economic impact of the conflict.
title: UK Studies Wider Ways to Help Economy on Iran, Starmer Says

description: President Donald Trump says he did not want Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents to wear masks as they assist with security screenings at airports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump to Order National Guard to Airports If ICE Not Enough

author: Ben Bartenstein, Fiona MacDonald, Sam Dagher, Mirette Magdy
description: Just before US markets opened on Monday, President Donald Trump backed down from his threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure if it didn’t reopen the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours — pushed by the surge in energy prices and global market rout unleashed by the US-Israeli war on Tehran and hopes that fresh talks could yield a deal to end the conflict.
title: Trump Backs Off Iran Energy Strike Threat as Markets Reel

description: US Energy Secretary Chris Wright says oil from the US strategic reserve started flowing on Friday afternoon. "Prices have not risen high enough yet to drive meaningful demand destruction,” Wright said during a discussion at CERA Week in Houston. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Oil From US Reserves Started Flowing Friday, Says Energy Secretary Wright

author: Donato Paolo Mancini
description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is on track to narrowly lose a national referendum to overhaul Italy’s judicial system, which has become a vote on the leader herself.
title: Meloni Faces Defeat in Italian Referendum on the Judiciary

author: Lydia Beyoud
description: The Securities and Exchange Commission sent two new proposed rules, one on digital assets and another on hedge fund and private equity firm disclosures, to the White House for review.
title: White House Reviewing SEC’s Crypto, Hedge Fund Disclosure Plans

author: Zoe Tillman
description: The Trump administration asked the US Supreme Court to block a government watchdog group from questioning a senior official and obtaining internal records about the Department of Government Efficiency project once led by Elon Musk.
title: Trump Administration Asks Supreme Court to Halt DOGE Inquiry

author: Hadriana Lowenkron, Natalie Lung
description: President Donald Trump said he did not want Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents detailed to airports to wear masks as they assist with security screenings — even as he continued to support officers using face coverings during deportation operations.
title: Trump Says ICE Agents Shouldn’t Wear Masks on Airport Duty

author: Yuliya Fedorinova
description: Russia’s steel industry is emerging as a new pain point for the Kremlin, with major producers beginning to shut capacity in the face of slowing domestic demand and limited export options.
title: Russian Steel Is Kremlin’s New Headache as Top Group Idles Units

author: Foster Wong
description: President Xi Jinping called for Xiong’an New Area to play a leading role in advancing innovative policies in sectors like technology and finance, reaffirming his commitment to develop a high-tech hub near Beijing.
title: Xi Urges New Flagship City to Lead Tech, Finance Policy Trials

author: Vanessa Perdomo
description: Iran’s national football team has said it won’t be attending the World Cup that kicks off in the US in June after President Donald Trump said the squad’s safety could not be assured.
title: What Happens If Iran Fails to Show Up at the World Cup?

author: Lucille Liu, Wenjin Lv
description: China plans to increase the amount of money that approved investors can channel into overseas assets as Beijing loosens its control over capital outflows.
title: China to Issue New Quotas for Investing Overseas, Official Says

author: Charlie Duxbury
description: Sweden’s government said it will temporarily cut the duty on vehicle fuels to reduce the inflationary impact of the Iran war on voters six months ahead of a general election.
title: Sweden Proposes to Cut Fuel Tax and Reduce Iran War Price Impact

author: John Bowker
description: US President Donald Trump said strikes against Iranian energy infrastructure and power plants would be postponed for five days following the start of talks with Iran to end the war.
title: Trump Backs Off From Iran Threat as Ceasefire Talks Get Underway

author: Hadriana Lowenkron
description: President Donald Trump put his threat to destroy Iranian power plants on hold for five days after what he described as “productive” talks with that country, sending oil down sharply and stocks soaring.
title: Trump Postpones Strikes Against Iran Power For Five Days

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: The focus on war over affordability is threatening the administration’s control over Washington
title: Trump’s Populist Approach Is Increasingly Out of Touch

author: James Mayger
description: After more than eight years of talks, Canberra and Brussels could finally agree on a trade deal.
title: EU and Australia Bind Together in Global Storm

author: Marie Gottschalk
description: The failure to prosecute elite wrongdoing is a bipartisan trend that’s hastening under Trump.
title: The Trump Administration Turns a Blind Eye to White-Collar Crime

author: Zoltan Simon
description: Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban is looking to mobilize support from European Union far-right leaders as his government battles allegations of Russian attempts to tilt the country’s pivotal elections in favor of the nationalist incumbent.
title: Orban Rallies Far-Right Allies Amid Russian Meddling Claims

author: Shinhye Kang
description: The influential sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un rejected Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s reported interest in holding a summit with Kim, saying talks wouldn’t happen simply because Japan wants them.
title: Kim’s Sister Rules Out Pyongyang Summit With Japan’s Takaichi

author: Anup Roy, Rajesh Roy
description: India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the country has sufficient energy supplies to meet domestic demand, even as he warned the Iran conflict creates unprecedented challenges for the world’s fastest growing large economy.
title: Modi Seeks to Calm India as Iran War Causes Acute Gas Shortage

author: Amanda Mull
description: Vibe-coded dashboards elevate the online news scroll to a different level.
title: We’re All Just ‘Monitoring the Situation’

author: Michael Nienaber, Arne Delfs
description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s effort to reboot Germany’s economy ran into a fresh challenge after his Social Democratic coalition partners suffered a stinging election defeat in a party stronghold.
title: Merz’s Win in SPD Stronghold Means Trouble for German Coalition

author: Gregory Viscusi, Alan Katz
description: Lionel Jospin, the former Socialist prime minister who introduced France’s 35-hour work week before trailing in third when far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen made the presidential runoff in 2002, has died, Agence France-Presse reported. He was 88.
title: Lionel Jospin, French Prime Minister Under Chirac, Dies Aged 88

description: Oil gained from the highest close since mid-2022, as investors assessed US President Donald Trump’s two-day deadline to Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran warned it would attack key infrastructure across the Middle East if Trump followed through. Bloomberg’s Will Kennedy reports.
title: Oil Higher as Trump Gives Iran Two-Day Hormuz Deadline

description: Bloomberg Businessweek hosts an exclusive roundtable with prominent Black business leaders to discuss DEI rollbacks in corporate America. Guests include Ursula Burns, Integrum Founding Partner, Lisa Wardell, American Express Board Director, Jacob Walthour, Jr., Blueprint Capital Advisors CEO, Nicole Reboe, Rich Talent Group CEO,  and Chris Williams, Siebert Williams Shank & Co. Chairman. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Businessweek Convenes: Black Leaders Face the DEI Backlash

description: Marine Le Pen’s party fell short in its bid to take control of a host of major French cities in Sunday’s municipal elections. The National Rally was defeated in a handful of large municipalities it targeted, including Marseille, Toulon and Nimes. A far-right candidate aligned with Le Pen won in Nice, the fifth-largest city in France. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports.
title: France’s Far Right Falls Short in Municipal Elections

description:
Bloomberg Daybreak Europe is your essential morning viewing to stay ahead. 

On today's show. US President Donald Trump issued Iran an ultimatum on Saturday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days or have its power plants bombed. Tehran threatened to “completely” close the corridor if attacked.

Asian stocks fell, Treasuries tumbled and gold sank in a selloff across assets after the US and Iran upped the ante in a war now in its fourth week.

German conservatives led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz have secured an election win in a state held by the Social Democrats for 35 years. Meanwhile, in France, the far-right fell short of taking control of some major cities during Sunday's municipal elections.

LaGuardia Airport was closed to incoming flights after an Air Canada Express flight
collided with a vehicle shortly after landing.

Today's guests: Jefferies economist Modupe Adegbembo & Salzgitter CEO Gunnar Groebler (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Iran War: Trump’s 48-Hour Iran Hormuz Deadline & Global Market Selloff | Daybreak Europe 3/23/2026

description: Rescue workers at the site of an Iranian missile strike in Arad, southern Israel, on March 22. Photographer: Kobi Wolf/Bloomberg
title: Trump Postpones Strikes on Iran Energy Targets

description: Israel launched a wave of airstrikes on infrastructure in Tehran and said it’s preparing to expand ground operations in Lebanon, where it’s fighting Iran-aligned Hezbollah. Defense Minister Israel Katz said at the weekend that the intensity of Israeli and US military attacks on Iran and its infrastructure would “increase significantly” in the coming week. Bloomberg’s Dan Williams reports.
title: IDF Says It Started Wide-Scale Strikes on Infrastructure

author: Patrick Sykes, Dana Khraiche
description: Iran carried out fresh strikes across the Persian Gulf hours before US President Donald Trump’s deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz expires, as the waterway’s closure continues to rattle global energy markets.
title: Iran Strikes Gulf Targets as Trump’s Hormuz Deadline Approaches

description: Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s Christian Democratic Union secured 31% of the vote in Rhineland-Palatinate, ahead of the Social Democrats with 25.9%, according to preliminary results. The victory softens the blow of a stinging defeat for the CDU in a state election in neighboring Baden-Wuerttemberg two weeks ago, but will still pile pressure on Merz’s coalition with the Social Democrats at the national level. Bloomberg’s Oliver Crook reports.
title: Merz’s CDU Secures Win in Southwestern German State

description: Police investigate antisemitic hate crime after ambulances set alight in LondonBy Jessica Coates and Rob Freeman, Press Association
title: Police Investigate Antisemitic Hate Crime After Ambulances Set On Fire

author: Mark Schroers
description: The European Central Bank is on alert for the fallout on prices from the Iran war, Vice President Luis de Guindos told El Mundo newspaper.
title: ECB Alert to Second-Round Effects From Iran War, Guindos Says

author: Sara Sjolin, Sanne Wass, Christian Wienberg
description: A controversial wealth tax on the rich, lifting a four-decade ban on nuclear power and the future of wind-farm developer Orsted A/S are all in the spotlight in Denmark’s national election on Tuesday.
title: Wealth Tax on the Rich and Nuclear Power: Investor Guide to Danish Vote

description: A selloff in stocks, gold and bonds deepened as the US and Iran hardened their rhetoric and signaled a potential escalation to their conflict, which is entering its fourth week. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US-Iran Rhetoric Intensifies as Stocks, Bonds Fall

description: Premier Li Qiang pledged to address worries that trade partners have about China’s large surplus, underscoring Beijing’s concern the issue could disrupt relations with more nations during a truce with the US in the tariff dispute. Bloomberg's Stephen Engle reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: China’s Premier Vows to Back Balanced Trade

author: Anthony Halpin
description: A Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Baltic Sea port of Primorsk, one of the country’s key oil export hubs, has damaged a fuel tank, according to local authorities.
title: Russia’s Primorsk Oil Port Hit by Drones With Fuel Tank on Fire

description: Macquarie University's Associate Professor Adam Lockyer warns of escalation as the Iran conflict enters its fourth week. It follows President Trump’s 48-hour deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face strikes on its power plants. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US ‘Speeding Past Off Ramps’ in Iran War: Expert

author: Matthew Burgess
description: Emerging-market assets declined as President Donald Trump’s ultimatum to Iran raised the risk of further disruptions to Middle East energy supplies.
title: Emerging-Market Assets Slip After Trump’s Ultimatum to Iran

author: Yoshiaki Nohara
description: A majority of Japanese people oppose sending warships to the Middle East in response to the war in Iran, according to two polls conducted over the weekend amid continued US pressure on allies to help secure the Strait of Hormuz.
title: Majority of Japanese Oppose Sending Warships to Middle East

description: Martin Sorrell, Executive Chairman at S4 Capital, says equity investors are not yet fully pricing in the impact of the war in Iran. He also says that prospects for a protracted conflict and higher oil prices are rattling the global executives he's been talking with. He speaks with Stephen Engle at the China Development Forum in Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: S4 Capital's Sorrell on Geopolitical Impact on Markets

description: Martin Sorrell, Executive Chairman at S4 Capital, says equity investors are not yet fully pricing in the impact of the war in Iran. He also says that prospects for a protracted conflict and higher oil prices are rattling the global executives he's been talking with. He speaks with Stephen Engle at the China Development Forum in Beijing. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: S4 Capital's Sorrell on Geopolitical Impact on Markets

description: US President Donald Trump gave Iran a two-day deadline to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or have its power plants bombed, upping the ante in a war that’s showing no sign of de-escalation into its fourth week. Bloomberg's Laura Davison shares what we know about the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump and Iran Hurl War Threats As Hormuz Crisis Builds
